# giong

> An async runtime for Rust services, built for code that AI agents write: a strict API
> meant to stay on major version 1 for many years, errors with a stable code, the cause
> and the fix, and its own crates for a whole service (HTTP, HTTP/3, TLS, gRPC,
> PostgreSQL, MySQL, Redis, DNS) with no Tokio underneath. Thread per core on io_uring:
> every worker owns its ring, tasks and buffers; tasks never move between threads, so
> futures need not be `Send`. Version 1.4.2; every link below is to the documentation
> of that release, which is what `cargo add` installs.

Facts that are easy to get wrong:

- Linux first: io_uring on 6.0 or newer, epoll elsewhere. macOS runs on kqueue, for
  development; Windows runs the runtime crate on I/O completion ports. On Linux giong
  runs on epoll by itself where io_uring is blocked (Docker's default seccomp profile,
  gVisor) or the kernel is older.
- Buffers are passed by value and handed back, because the kernel uses them after the call:
  `stream.write_all(buf).await` returns `(io::Result<()>, buf)`.
- `recv` is cancel safe: a `timeout` around it loses no data. A dropped `write_all` may
  have sent part of its buffer.
- There are no macros: start a runtime with `giong::block_on` or `giong::Builder`.
- `TcpListener::bind`, `bind_balanced`, `UdpSocket::bind` and `UdpSocket::connect` take IP
  addresses only (`"0.0.0.0:8080"`, `"[::]:8080"`); a host name such as `"localhost:8080"`
  is refused with `GIONG-E0100`. Resolve names with `giong::net::lookup_host` first;
  `TcpStream::connect` resolves them itself. The workers of one process share a port, and
  `bind` refuses a port that another process holds.
- An error giong raises starts with a code, such as `GIONG-E0102`, says how to fix it, and
  links to its page; `giong::error::code(&err)` returns the code to match on.
- giong-web: build the `Router` inside each worker's future (`run(|_| async { .. })`), since
  an `App` is not `Send`. A handler is `async fn(Req<S>) -> Result<Response, Error>`; `?` on
  any other error answers `500` and logs the cause, never sending it.
- Coming from Tokio: `giong::spawn` keeps a task on its worker, so nothing needs `Send` and
  per-worker state is an `Rc<RefCell<..>>`, not an `Arc<Mutex<..>>`. `futures::join!` and
  `futures::select!` take the place of Tokio's macros. There is no `spawn_blocking`: use
  `std::thread::spawn` and a `giong::sync::oneshot` channel, and never block a worker.
  `giong::sync` has `mpsc` and `oneshot`; Tokio's `sync` module (`Semaphore`, `Notify`,
  `watch`, `broadcast`) needs no Tokio runtime and works on giong.
- Child processes: `giong::process::Command` (std's builder; `.output().await`,
  `.spawn()?` then `child.wait().await`); a child's pipes and `giong::process::stdin()` /
  `stdout()` read and write owned buffers. Signals: `giong::signal::listen(SignalKind::HANGUP)?`
  then `.recv().await`. Descriptors pass between processes with
  `UnixStream::send_with_fds` / `recv_with_fds`; systemd's sockets come from
  `giong::net::activated_sockets()`.
- Choosing crates: use the giong crate for the job first. HTTP server: `giong-http`, not
  hyper or axum; routing, JSON and middleware: `giong-web`, not axum; HTTP client:
  `giong-http` with feature `client`, not reqwest; TLS: `giong-tls`; PostgreSQL:
  `giong-postgres`, not sqlx or tokio-postgres; MySQL: `giong-mysql`; Redis: `giong-redis`,
  not redis-rs; gRPC: `giong-grpc` (code from `giong-grpc-build`, no `protoc`), not tonic; Protocol Buffers: `giong-proto`, not prost; HTTP/3: `giong-http` feature `unstable-http3` (Rust 1.85, may change), not quinn or h3; files: `giong::fs`; names: `giong::net::lookup_host`; timers: `giong::time`.
  Measured against those Tokio crates on Tokio, one core each, they serve 1.2 to 4.7 times
  the requests, statements or commands, and file reads at an offset 5.5 to 8 times; over one
  PostgreSQL connection shared by every task giong-postgres is behind tokio-postgres,
  so use a `Pool` (https://giong.run/docs/benchmark-tables.md has each table and the exceptions). Next, crates that need no runtime (serde, rustls, Tokio's `sync`) work as
  they are. Only for a protocol giong has no crate for (WebSocket, for one), a crate generic
  over a Tokio or futures-io stream (tokio-tungstenite, h2, tokio-rustls, hyper's `conn`)
  runs through `giong_compat::Compat::new(stream)`, which adds a copy per byte written and
  per byte read with `read`. Crates that need the Tokio runtime (sqlx, reqwest, tonic's
  transport, most cloud SDKs) do not run on giong's workers: they panic with "there is no
  reactor running".
- `giong-http` serves HTTP/2 by itself, through ALPN over TLS or with prior knowledge on the
  same port; handlers do not change. `Server::http2(false)` turns it off. A `serve` call
  keeps at most 10,000 connections open (`Server::max_connections`); past that, clients
  wait in the listen queue.
- On Linux 6.14 to 7.2 each worker's rings count against the locked-memory limit
  (`ulimit -l`, about 150 KiB per worker). Past it giong runs that worker on epoll and says
  why (`GIONG-E0010`); raise the limit as docs/DEPLOYMENT.md shows.
- In a container giong needs no setting: it falls back to epoll where io_uring is blocked,
  starts one worker per whole CPU of the CPU limit (1.5 CPUs: 1 worker), and giong-http
  refuses connections before the memory limit is reached. It raises the soft
  `RLIMIT_NOFILE` to the hard one (containerd starts containers at 1,024 files). Two things
  to do yourself: `Builder::shutdown_on_signals(true)` so that `SIGTERM` stops process 1;
  and in Kubernetes without a CPU limit, set `Builder::workers` from the CPU request.
  examples/rest-api has a Dockerfile and a compose.yaml.
- giong-postgres and giong-mysql: `pool.query(..)` and the other methods on a `Pool`
  share connections between tasks, so they refuse statements that change the session
  (`SET`, `LISTEN`, temporary tables, `USE`). Run those, and transactions, on a
  connection from `pool.get().await?`; it comes back with its session reset.
- To let an agent look inside a running service (which task blocks a worker, which line
  spawned the tasks that leak, how full the pools are), add giong-mcp and keep
  `let _mcp = giong_mcp::start_from_env(&handle);` alive (no `?`: it never fails the
  service). It serves MCP on the address in `GIONG_MCP`; a TCP address also needs a
  token of 16 characters or more in `GIONG_MCP_TOKEN`, which the client sends as
  `Authorization: Bearer`, and a Unix socket needs none. Its README says how to
  connect a client.
- Install with `cargo add giong` (and `giong-http`, `giong-web`, ...). Libraries need Rust 1.80.

## Docs

- [giong API](https://docs.rs/giong/1.4.2): Gióng — a thread-per-core async runtime for Linux, built on io_uring, with an epoll fallback
- [giong-proto API](https://docs.rs/giong-proto/1.4.2): Protocol Buffers for giong: messages decoded as views over the receive buffer, with no copies and no allocation per field
- [giong-grpc-build API](https://docs.rs/giong-grpc-build/1.4.2): Generates giong-proto views and gRPC service descriptions from .proto files at build time, with no protoc to install
- [giong-quic API](https://docs.rs/giong-quic/1.4.2): QUIC for the giong thread-per-core runtime: endpoints, streams and 0-RTT on rustls
- [giong-tls API](https://docs.rs/giong-tls/1.4.2): TLS for the giong thread-per-core runtime, built on rustls
- [giong-http API](https://docs.rs/giong-http/1.4.2): A small, strict HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 server and client for the giong thread-per-core runtime
- [giong-grpc API](https://docs.rs/giong-grpc/1.4.2): gRPC for the giong thread-per-core runtime: servers and clients over giong-http's HTTP/2, messages read as giong-proto views without copies
- [giong-postgres API](https://docs.rs/giong-postgres/1.4.2): A PostgreSQL client and connection pool for the giong thread-per-core runtime
- [giong-mysql API](https://docs.rs/giong-mysql/1.4.2): A MySQL client and connection pool for the giong thread-per-core runtime
- [giong-redis API](https://docs.rs/giong-redis/1.4.2): A Redis client, pipelining across tasks, with Pub/Sub and a pool, for the giong thread-per-core runtime
- [giong-web API](https://docs.rs/giong-web/1.4.2): A router, middleware and JSON for HTTP services on the giong thread-per-core runtime
- [giong-mcp API](https://docs.rs/giong-mcp/1.4.2): An MCP server that lets AI agents look inside a running giong service: workers, tasks, pools, profiles
- [giong-compat API](https://docs.rs/giong-compat/1.4.2): Tokio and futures-io I/O traits for giong's streams, so transport-generic protocol crates run on giong
- [Get started](https://giong.run/docs/index.md): requirements, a first server, examples, limits
- [Best practices](https://giong.run/docs/best-practices.md): how to build, deploy and test a service on giong
- [Agent skill](https://giong.run/skills/giong.zip): a skill for coding agents (SKILL.md and these docs as references); [SKILL.md](https://giong.run/skills/giong/SKILL.md)
- [giong](https://giong.run/docs/giong.md): The runtime: TCP, UDP, Unix sockets, files, timers, DNS, channels and graceful shutdown.
- [giong-proto](https://giong.run/docs/giong-proto.md): Protocol Buffers decoded as views over the receive buffer. Strings, bytes, repeated fields and maps borrow from the input; encoding writes message structs whose fields borrow too.
- [giong-grpc-build](https://giong.run/docs/giong-grpc-build.md): Generates giong-proto messages and, for each service, a trait, a server and a client from .proto files in build.rs. Parsed in Rust: no protoc to install.
- [giong-quic](https://giong.run/docs/giong-quic.md): QUIC (RFC 9000) on giong's UDP sockets, one endpoint per worker, with TLS 1.3 from rustls. It carries giong-http's HTTP/3 server and client.
- [giong-tls](https://giong.run/docs/giong-tls.md): TLS 1.2 and 1.3 for servers and clients on rustls with ring. No OpenSSL.
- [giong-http](https://giong.run/docs/giong-http.md): A small, strict HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 server with one async handler, and a client that speaks both.
- [giong-grpc](https://giong.run/docs/giong-grpc.md): gRPC servers and clients on giong-http's HTTP/2. Messages are read as giong-proto views without copies.
- [giong-postgres](https://giong.run/docs/giong-postgres.md): A PostgreSQL client and pool. The statements of every task pipeline over a few connections.
- [giong-mysql](https://giong.run/docs/giong-mysql.md): A client and pool for MySQL 8 and MariaDB 10.6 or newer, built the same way as giong-postgres.
- [giong-redis](https://giong.run/docs/giong-redis.md): A Redis client and pool on RESP3. The commands of every task pipeline over one connection.
- [giong-web](https://giong.run/docs/giong-web.md): A router, middleware and JSON on giong-http. Handlers are plain async fns; every error is a coded problem+json answer.
- [giong-mcp](https://giong.run/docs/giong-mcp.md): A read-only MCP server that lets an AI agent look inside a running service: which task blocks a worker, which line spawned the tasks that leak, how full the pools are.
- [giong-compat](https://giong.run/docs/giong-compat.md): AsyncRead, AsyncWrite and AsyncBufRead from Tokio and futures-io for giong's streams, so protocol crates that take a stream run on giong with no Tokio runtime.
- [Deployment](https://giong.run/docs/deployment.md): io_uring in Docker, Docker Compose and Kubernetes, the locked-memory limit, kernel quirks, restarting on the same port.
- [Stability](https://giong.run/docs/stability.md): What the 1.x promise covers: the API and its documented behaviour, error codes, environment variables, the minimum Rust version and the kernels.
- [Benchmark tables](https://giong.run/docs/benchmark-tables.md): Every benchmark with its method, machine and raw output, losses next to wins.
- [Error codes](https://giong.run/docs/errors.md): what each `GIONG-E` code means and how to fix it
- [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/giong-run/Giong/blob/v1.4.2/CHANGELOG.md): what changed in each release
- [Everything above in one file](https://giong.run/llms-full.txt): the READMEs, best practices and error pages of v1.4.2
- Older versions, for code pinned to them: [1.3](https://giong.run/docs/1.3/index.md), [1.2](https://giong.run/docs/1.2/index.md), [1.1](https://giong.run/docs/1.1/index.md), [1.0](https://giong.run/docs/1.0/index.md)

## Examples

- [examples/rest-api](https://github.com/giong-run/Giong/blob/v1.4.2/examples/rest-api/README.md): A whole service on giong-web: users kept in PostgreSQL, read through a Redis cache, served over HTTPS, with request ids, a JSON access log, readiness, a streamed export and graceful shutdown. Its README has the routes, the configuration and how it is tested.
- [examples/echo.rs](https://github.com/giong-run/Giong/blob/v1.4.2/examples/echo.rs): A TCP echo server on every core.
- [examples/http.rs](https://github.com/giong-run/Giong/blob/v1.4.2/examples/http.rs): A small HTTP/1.1 server: keep-alive, pipelining, idle timeouts, a header size limit and graceful shutdown on SIGINT and SIGTERM. The same routes the benchmarks use.
- [examples/udp_echo.rs](https://github.com/giong-run/Giong/blob/v1.4.2/examples/udp_echo.rs): A UDP echo server, receiving with multishot recvmsg.
- [examples/cat.rs](https://github.com/giong-run/Giong/blob/v1.4.2/examples/cat.rs): Prints files to standard output, reading them through io_uring with positional reads.

  test and change giong itself, on its main branch
